To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

rats learn to discriminate a contingency between a lever press and an interruption in a previously established tone before they learn to refrain from pressing the lever before the interruption, and that this discrimination is reflected in a differential latency of the first post-interruption press.

rats learn to refrain from lever pressing before a brief interruption of tone, and that they do not learn to do this until after they learn to discriminate between trials with and without reinforcement.

rats learn to discriminate between trials in which they have and in which they have not pressed the lever before the interruption, and that they learn this discrimination before they reliably refrain from pressing the lever before the tone interruption.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the temporal aspects of behavior, and with the relation between the temporal properties of behavior and reinforcement.
the role of temporal properties of behavior in learning.
the temporal properties of behavior and the way in which these are related to learning.

the present finding shows that memory of the temporal properties of one's behavior is a necessary but not sufficient condition for learning to carry out that behavior.
the temporal properties are a necessary but not sufficient condition for learning to carry out a behavior that meets a contingency.

the present results show that the rats learned that their behavior had to meet a contingency, but that they did not learn to meet it, at least not in the sense of learning to refrain from pressing the lever before the interruption.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

rats can learn to discriminate between a tone interruption that signals reward and one that signals no reward; they can learn to press a lever before the interruption if it signals reward and not to press if it does not; and, in the latter case, they can learn to refrain from pressing after a brief interruption if it signals no reward.
the temporal properties that are learned and stored are not the same as those that are used in behavior.

the rat is able to remember the temporal properties of its recent behavior, but not the reinforcement-producing aspect, and that it can use this memory to discriminate between trials in which it is and is not about to be rewarded, and to adjust its behavior accordingly.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the rats' discrimination of impending reinforcement occurred before the animals reliably produced the behavior necessary for that reinforcement to occur.
the temporal properties in which rats can discriminate are much more fine-grained than those of which we were previously aware.
